key_concepts: Invertebrate body shapes can be bilateral, radial, or asymmetrical.
Arthropods have an exoskeleton, antennae, and simple or compound eyes.
Arachnids are eight-legged arthropods such as spiders and scorpions.
Crustaceans are ten-legged arthropods with compound eyes and a cephalothorax.
Insects are six-legged arthropods with antennae, compound eyes, and usually wings.
Mollusks are soft-bodied invertebrates with bilateral symmetry.
Poriferans, or sponges, are simple aquatic invertebrates with pores.
Echinoderms are spiny-skinned invertebrates such as sea stars and sea urchins.
Cnidarians are jelly-like invertebrates with radial symmetry and an internal cavity.
Worms are soft-bodied invertebrates that may be flat, round, or segmented.
